_note: The eight patient pages of the full Lovable export's Gap 2, as one contract: symptom-checker, risk-assessment, health-library, health-timeline, vaccinations, community, nutrition and reminders, plus the 'Your health' hub that carries them. Recorded by docs/design-review/LOVABLE-EXPORT-RECONCILIATION.md (Phase C) and built under the gates in docs/ROADMAP.md's Phase D. The web reads this file through apps/web/src/lib/patient-pages.ts; scripts/emit-patient-pages.mjs writes the router's two strings per page and the two native data files. Content rows are DERIVED from contracts that already exist — the knowledge base, the symptom intake, the SOS register — and the derivation is held by scripts/check-boundaries.mjs, so this file names sources and never copies their entries.
_rules: No screen renders a sentence that is not in this file or in the contract it derives from. No screen displays a number this tree's contracts do not hold: the 25 September ruling (option B) applies — structural and visual honesty, written empty states wherever a number would go. symptom-checker and risk-assessment inherit the screening capability's block: no model, no vendor, no licence. The symptom checker asks symptom-intake.json's set questions and escalates on the emergency words before anything else reads an answer; it sets no priority, names no cause and gives no advice, and the findings case.json works out are for the nurse and never rendered here. Knowledge content shows its own source line and the review notice below sits beside it until a clinician has signed.

changelog.what: The eight pages and their hub, from the full Lovable export's Phase D, with every derivation named.

review.notice: This page carries general health information that no registered clinician has signed yet. Your nurse's advice comes first.
review.why: The same posture as care-tips.json: the frame is built and gated, the knowledge entries carry their own sources, and one clinical reviewer must sign before a real patient relies on any of it. Until then every screen in this contract shows this notice.

symptom-checker.heading: Tell us what is wrong.
symptom-checker.lead: This is not a diagnosis and it does not score you. It asks the same set questions GilbertOne asks, one at a time, and writes your answers down as a note you hand to your nurse.

emergency.heading: Stop — this sounds like an emergency.
emergency.detail: The emergency words come first, before any note is taken. The ambulance number and the crisis lines are on the emergency screen.

handover.heading: Your notes are ready.
handover.detail: Nothing is stored and nothing is sent while the identity service is off — there is no account to attach a note to yet. Copy the notes or read them to your nurse at the visit; GilbertOne's intake keeps the same card.

symptom-checker.stoppedNote: You stopped early. The answers so far are on the card, and a nurse would rather have half the note than none of it.

risk-assessment.heading: A risk assessment needs a clinician, not a formula.
risk-assessment.lead: MyThuso does not compute a risk score. Screening is blocked until there is a model, a vendor and a licence, and a validated score is a clinical judgement this product refuses to fake.

blocked.heading: Why this page has no score
blocked.detail: A number here would be read as a verdict about your health. Nothing in this tree holds one: no screening model is licensed, no clinician has ratified a scoring rule, and the frame around a result — provenance, sign-off, conflict resolution — exists precisely so that a score is never shown without them.

wouldCover.heading: What a ratified assessment would cover

rows.title: Your own readings
rows.detail: Vitals from a Thuso Kit, validated against the ranges the records contract holds — once a device is paired to a real account.

rows.title: What a clinician finds
rows.detail: A nurse's assessment and a doctor's review, each signed, each with the day and the registration on file.

rows.title: What changes over time
rows.detail: Trends across visits, on the Health Passport, where the record actually lives.

health-library.heading: Trusted guidance, in plain language.
health-library.lead: Every entry is from the governed South African knowledge base this tree already carries, with the authority it came from beside it. It is general information about health, never advice about you.
health-library.emptyDetail: Try one word — a condition, a medicine, or 'clinic'.

health-timeline.heading: One line, from your first visit to today.
health-timeline.lead: The timeline is a view of the Health Passport — the record service holds the entries, and this page will read them the day the Passport's record service is out of development-only gating. Until then it shows the kinds of entry it will carry, and nothing invented.

kinds.title: Visits and assessments
kinds.detail: Every nurse visit, its summary and the doctor's reviews of it.

kinds.title: Readings
kinds.detail: Vitals from your Thuso Kit, each with the device it came from.

kinds.title: Medicine and dispensing
kinds.detail: Prescriptions, collections and repeats, from the medicines contract.

kinds.title: Laboratory results
kinds.detail: Released results only, each with the day it was released and by whom.

kinds.title: Consents and access
kinds.detail: Who you shared with, what scope, and every time a record was opened.

health-timeline.emptyDetail: Nothing is written to a timeline in a design preview: the records live in the Passport's development service and no real patient data exists to read. When the service is live, this line fills from it and from nothing else.

vaccinations.heading: The South African schedule, and your own record.
vaccinations.lead: The schedule below is the knowledge base's immunisation material — the public EPI schedule and the entries beside it — with the authority named on every card. Your personal vaccination record is the empty state underneath it, honestly.

record.heading: Your vaccination record
record.emptyDetail: Your own doses belong on the Health Passport, and the Passport's service is in development-only gating — no real record exists to show. A vaccination you invent on a screen is a vaccination a nurse might trust, so this stays empty until the record is real.

vaccinations.roadToHealth: A child's doses are also recorded on the Road to Health card the clinic gives at birth — keep it with the birth certificate.

community.heading: Help that does not need a visit.
community.lead: Public clinics, helplines and the health system's own navigation material, from the knowledge base. What is not here yet is a community of people: that needs accounts and messaging, and both are off.
community.helplinesNote: These lines are the knowledge base's own entries, with their sources. The emergency number is on the emergency screen and is never restated here.

notConnected.heading: Groups and neighbours are not connected
notConnected.detail: A community feed needs the identity service and a messaging provider. Neither exists yet, so rather than a simulated feed this page shows what is real: the public system's own material.

nutrition.heading: General guidance, from the governed base.
nutrition.lead: The entries below are the knowledge base's nutrition, lifestyle and feeding material — prevention, maternal and chronic care — each with its source. None of it is a meal plan for you: a diet that treats a condition is a clinician's, not a screen's.
refusals: It does not write a meal plan for a condition — that is a clinician's or a registered dietitian's.
It does not name amounts, doses or targets for you; the numbers in an entry are the general ones its source published.
It does not replace the advice on your care plan or from your nurse.

reminders.heading: Reminders need an account, and accounts are off.
reminders.lead: A reminder is a promise about a real day — your visit, your collection, your check-in. The identity service is deliberately switched off until there is an SMS provider, so nothing here can promise anything yet. What follows is what the page will carry, from the contracts that already hold those events.

kinds.title: Before a visit
kinds.detail: The booking contract's own confirmations and the day-before note, to the phone that booked it.

kinds.title: Medicine collection
kinds.detail: When a prescription is ready and when a repeat is due, from the dispensing contract.

kinds.title: Care plan check-ins
kinds.detail: The routine a plan names — the adherence nudge the funding proposal asks for — on the plan's own cadence.

kinds.title: After a visit
kinds.detail: The visit summary, and the care tips that follow it.

reminders.emptyDetail: Nothing is scheduled because no account exists to schedule against. This is the intended state, not a fault: reminders arrive with the identity service, and not before.

derivations._why: Each list a screen renders from another contract, named here so the build can hold the two to each other: every derivation must resolve, and a source that stops carrying what is named here fails the build rather than rendering an empty screen that looks finished.

emergencyNumbers.note: rendered by the emergency screen this page opens, never restated here

refusals.sentence: Nothing here diagnoses, scores or triages you. A diagnosis is a clinician's, and screening stays blocked until a model, a vendor and a licence exist.
No screen shows a number this tree's contracts do not hold. Where a figure would go, a written empty state says what is missing and why.
The library, nutrition and vaccination material is general information with its source beside it — never advice about you. Your nurse's advice comes first.
The emergency words are read before any of it. An emergency answer ends the screen and opens the emergency pathway with 10177 first.

platformsWhy: Web first, as with care-tips and the case pathway: the screens are the frame the founder asked to see, and the generated Swift and Kotlin data files carry every word so the native screens are a later wave's assembly rather than a rewrite. symptom-intake.json's own platforms list stays as it is until a native screen renders it.
